front: Effect of adding k / multiplying by k on data?
back: +k: mean +k, spread same. ×k: mean ×k, SD and IQR ×k, variance ×k².

front: Estimating a mean from grouped data?

back: Mean: $\bar x = \frac{\sum x}n$. Median: middle value of the ordered data (position $\frac{n+1}2$). Mode: most frequent value.
$IQR = Q_3 - Q_1$, the spread of the middle 50% of the data.
SD $\sigma$: typical distance of values from the mean. Variance $= \sigma^2$. In IB, find them with a GDC ($\sigma_x$).

front: Which measures are affected by outliers?
back: Mean, range and standard deviation are affected; median and IQR are resistant.

front: Data have mean 20 and SD 3. Each value is doubled then 5 added. New mean and SD?
back: Mean $2(20) + 5 = 45$; SD $2\times3 = 6$ (adding 5 does not change spread).

front: Does adding a constant to every value change the standard deviation?
back: No — every value moves equally, so SD, variance and IQR are unchanged; only the measures of centre shift.
$\bar x = \dfrac{n_1\bar x_1 + n_2\bar x_2}{n_1 + n_2}$ (total of all values ÷ total count).

front: Five values have mean 8; four of them are 6, 7, 9, 10. Find the fifth.
Modal class, and why is a grouped mean an estimate?
back: Modal class: the class with the highest frequency. The grouped mean uses midpoints, not the actual values, so it is only an estimate.
